feature: Appearance is what it is, Effects is what you add
summary: The panel now splits on one sentence. Appearance, straight under Layers, holds what a shape simply has: opacity, fill, outline, and a corner radius only where there are corners. Effects, under it, starts empty and is a list you add to, so a shape can carry two shadows and a blur, each removable, each with settings visibly its own.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Flags are on by default. Draw a rectangle with R and drag.

try.do: Draw a rectangle. Look at Appearance: Opacity, Fill, Outline with its Width, Corner Radius. Effects below it is empty.
Press the plus on the Effects header and read the menu: Shadow, Inner Shadow, Blur.
Choose Shadow, then press the plus again and choose Shadow a second time.
Press the plus once more and choose Blur. The Blur row lands at the top and the box goes soft.
Pull Shadow 2's Distance and Direction so the two shadows sit apart, then drag Shadow 2's grip above Shadow 1 and watch which one is on top.
Untick the Blur row: the box sharpens and the Amount stays where you left it. Tick it again.
Press the cross on the Blur row. The row goes, and Effects is two shadows.
Draw an ellipse. Appearance shows no Corner Radius, because an ellipse has no corners.

evaluate: Can you say in one sentence which panel a thing belongs in, without being told?
Reading Shadow 1's Softness, is it obvious it belongs to that shadow and not to the layer?
Is an empty Effects section with one line of text and a plus enough of an invitation, or does it need something more?
Opacity now leads Appearance and Corner Radius closes it. Is that the order your hand expects?
Appearance and Effects moved above the section named after what you picked (Rectangle, Text). Was that the right trade?
The Blur row has no grip because a blur is laid over the whole layer. Does that read as deliberate, or as missing?
rough: A border with an offset, so an inner and an outer one are two rows, is NOT built. Nothing in the app can paint outside a layer's own edge yet: the shape rasterizer would need padding and the layer's reach would have to grow with it. Filed as a-border-can-sit-outside-the-edge-not-only-insid, and it is the only part of the brief that is missing.

Two shadows and a blur is already taller than the Effects section, so it scrolls inside itself and fades at the bottom edge. Appearance is whole; Effects is the one that gives. That is the right way round now, but a shadow still costs seven rows and that is a lot.
The shadow's own softness was called Blur and is now called Softness, because a row called Blur can sit directly above it. Only in Next.
The order of the list is real between shadows and nowhere else yet: a blur is pinned to the top and carries no grip. When a glow arrives it will be draggable like a shadow.
The grip cannot be driven by a script (a synthesized press cannot start a SwiftUI drag), so reordering was checked through the row's right-click menu and by test rather than by the drag itself.
Screen Recording was granted, so every picture here is a real capture of the window.
